title: Why More Context Makes Your Agent Dumber and What to Do About It — Nupur Sharma, Qodo
talk_summary: The speaker argues that large context windows do not fix agent focus: models attend to the start and end and lose middle context, so teams should optimize context rather than dump everything. She recommends iterative retrieval, 80/20 model routing with hard gates, specialized agents plus a judge, and review calibration from PR history and acceptance feedback.

takeaways.technique: Iterative retrieval index instead of full context dump
takeaways.evidence_quote: iterative retrieval works really good because instead of even creating a summary it creates kind of an index

takeaways.what_they_do: They let strong reasoning models do open-ended discovery/planning, then use cheaper or more deterministic steps for final validation and summarization, with counters/timeouts to stop loops.
A context collector splits PR context to specialized agents such as security, code-diff, and Jira agents; a judge agent then filters and combines their findings for relevance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a judge agent actually looks for the results and say okay these are interesting enough but is it relevant to you

takeaways.what_they_do: They index past PRs and whether developers accepted or rejected review suggestions, then weight future findings; explicit rules are always surfaced.
They avoid giving one agent multiple tasks because it tends to focus on some tasks and lose others; they use small expert agents for specific tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: maybe you give four tasks to the agent and somewhere down the line it focuses on two tasks

takeaways.what_they_do: A critic node checks whether the agent’s output still matches the original goal and triggers a retry if context was lost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a critic node which looks and say if that is relevant to your initial goal or not
